events.what: Fox and Hunter prove three-colour van der Waerden numbers w(k;3) grow super-exponentially via an explicit colouring of {1,...,2^{k·log*(k)/4}}
Campos, Fox and Schildkraut prove w(k) ≥ (1−o(1))k·2^(k−1) for all k, Erdős's 1968 conjectured lower bound, via a colouring found by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro
events.ai_basis: The coloring used to prove Theorem 1, as well as a proof of Theorem 1, were generated by a query to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro. The proof we present, while drawing somewhat on the proof given by ChatGPT, was produced by the authors ... All of the writing is our own.

events.what: Karki reports canonical/mixed van der Waerden number w(21; 2^17,3^2) = 52 (U(t)-Mathazine, Summer 2024)
events.credibility_reason: Primary source not located; known only via Wikipedia citation; year-only 2024 date cannot be placed relative to 26 January.

judgement.doubts: Both 2026 events are bounds on different quantities (3-colour growth; 2-colour lower bound), so neither supersedes the other and the tier is progress. The AI role between assisted and generated is a close call: the colouring, which is the construction giving the bound, and a first proof came from ChatGPT; the authors rewrote the proof. The abstract says 'It was found by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro.' The Karki exact value is one mixed canonical number, a single instance of a different notion, and cannot count.

corrections.why: F9: the record quotes the authors saying 'The coloring used to prove Theorem 1, as well as a proof of Theorem 1, were generated by a query to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro', and the abstract says 'It was found by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro.' The construction in the final result is the model's, and the humans rewrote and checked its proof. That fits 'generated' (the AI produced the construction and proof, and people checked it). The authors rewriting the proof is presentation, not new mathematics. This was close; see competing_reading.

F3: kept. The bullet asks for the values, and both preprints give asymptotic bounds without fixing any value. Proving Erdős's lower-bound conjecture is still a bound on w(k), not a determination of it.
